### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-settings`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s).

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/settings-service.mdx`  _(via SettingsContext (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via authGate (symbol, a field of interface SettingsContext))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/config-resolution.mdx`  _(via registerSettingsRoutes (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **9** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 99e944daf26ac1d2d50e90c5b631349ab45f664f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `dad54a2d73e23aefd14858cf421dfd33a6088f69` — the merge of head `8a0e89368c4b2ef4a5959766a1a14d85e99e8a98` into base `99e944daf26ac1d2d50e90c5b631349ab45f664f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin dad54a2d73e23aefd14858cf421dfd33a6088f69 && git checkout dad54a2d73e23aefd14858cf421dfd33a6088f69
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 99e944daf26ac1d2d50e90c5b631349ab45f664f 8a0e89368c4b2ef4a5959766a1a14d85e99e8a98 && git checkout -B drift-repro 99e944daf26ac1d2d50e90c5b631349ab45f664f && git merge --no-ff 8a0e89368c4b2ef4a5959766a1a14d85e99e8a98

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 99e944daf26ac1d2d50e90c5b631349ab45f664f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 99e944daf26ac1d2d50e90c5b631349ab45f664f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8a0e89368c4b2ef4a5959766a1a14d85e99e8a98`
Local-runs: none

**Inputs read:** card #23178 (body; all thirteen comments, 6139290291 through 6147724004, including triage's direction 6142961139, the seat's landing and release 6142709445, the dispatch 6146033345, the dev report 6147674138 and the seat ACCEPT 6147724004); PR #23285 (body; the one bot comment 6147651038; the 5-file list; the net diff against `main` from merge base `6d7f4df3c9`, +512 / -6; the three commits); PR #23200's body and its contract review 6142166159, plus the four sibling doors read at the merge commit `08b38cb9d8`; `origin/main` at `99e944daf2` for `packages/core/src/security/auth-gate.ts`, `security/index.ts`, `resolve-authz-context.ts`, REST's `enforceAuth` and `computeExecCtx`, the dispatcher's `enforceAuthGate`, plugin-auth's `customSession` enrichment with `computeAuthGate` and `isAuthGateActive`, ADR-0069, and `service-settings` (routes, plugin, types, barrel, package manifest, route ledger); the check-runs on the head, read until every `Test Core` shard had concluded. Read-only throughout: the branch fetched into an owned ref, REST reads, nothing built, run or re-run. No governed surface in the file list; the head repo is the base repo; the PR is draft; 518 changed lines.

**Check-runs on the head (last read 2026-10-13T14:30Z):** 39 runs; 28 conclude `success`, 6 `skipped` (the full-battery jobs a PR run does not carry), 0 red. Of the five required contexts, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Build Core` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` conclude `success`; `Test Core` had not concluded at this read: shard 6/6 `success`, shards 1 through 5 still `in_progress`, reported as such and not assumed. `Check Changeset`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, both single-writer guards and the two card-form guards conclude `success`. This record is the contract verdict on the head; the landing still waits on the owning seat reading every required context green, per the queue rule.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies, each judged:

1. **The public surface moves by exactly one optional member, and it is core's existing type.** `SettingsContext` (declared in `settings-service.types.ts`, re-exported by name from the package barrel, which the diff does not touch) gains `authGate?: AuthGate`, with `AuthGate` imported type-only from `@objectstack/core`, where it is derived from `ExecutionContext`'s declared `authGate` and exported through `security/index.ts` and the root barrel. No other exported declaration moves: `registerSettingsRoutes`, `SettingsRoutesOptions`, `SettingsServicePlugin` and the barrel are unchanged; the new door function `refuseHeldSession` is module-private; `ErrorCode` is a type-only import from a package the manifest already depends on. **Right.** The dev's built-declaration reading (the member, the import line, a docblock, one union printed in another order with the same members) is consistent with this source reading and was not reproduced here. The one mention of `SettingsContext` outside the package (REST's settings-slot docblock) describes its argument structurally and is unaffected.

2. **The door consults the gate through core's exports, with no copy of the allow-list or of the decision.** `refuseHeldSession` calls `evaluateAuthGate(ctx, '')` and answers `sendError(res, 403, gate.code, gate.message)`; `evaluateAuthGate` itself runs `normalizeAuthGate` and `isAuthGateAllowlisted`, both core's. The module restates no route, base, method or allow-list rule and reads no `isAuthGateAllowlisted` of its own. The resolver calls `normalizeAuthGate(sessionUser)` and spreads the result only when present, the same two lines the share-link resolver landed at `08b38cb9d8` uses. **Right.** One spelling note, not a defect: the datasource and storage doors hand `evaluateAuthGate` the session user and the share-link door reads `ctx.authGate` directly; this door hands it the resolved context, whose `authGate` the normalizer reads by the same name. All of them are a call of the shared decision.

3. **Order and answer match REST's `enforceAuth` and the four sibling doors.** `mountFamilyRoute` resolves the caller, asks `refuseHeldSession`, then `shouldDenyAnonymous`, then `serve`; REST's `enforceAuth` reads `context.authGate` first and the anonymous decision second; the datasource door orders `evaluateAuthGate` ahead of `shouldDenyAnonymous` the same way. The refusal is 403 with the gate's own `code` and `message`, through the family's declared `sendError` envelope, as the sibling doors answer it and as review 6142166159 accepted for them. The family's `catch` arm is untouched: an authorization-store outage the resolver raises is still relayed as its declared 503, and every other throw still takes the route's own `refuse`. REST skips `OPTIONS`; this family registers no `OPTIONS` route and no middleware (pinned by the census), so a preflight never reaches the door. **Right.**

4. **`evaluateAuthGate(ctx, '')`, the empty and so fail-closed path, is right for this family.** `isAuthGateAllowlisted('')` answers false by its own contract (#7898), so the empty path forfeits only an exemption no settings route could earn: the allow-list names the remediation surface, a few exact bootstrap reads, the approval act page and the inbound hook, and none of the four ledgered settings routes is one under any mount base (the ledger and the allow-list rows were read side by side). It is the reasoning the anonymous floor already applies in this file and the reasoning review 6142166159 accepted for all four siblings. The pin's allow-listed-base case carries a non-vacuity check that the predicate really would exempt that base if it were asked. **Right.**

5. **"No 503 arm" is right, read against REST's `computeExecCtx`.** REST's 503 (`AuthzStoreUnavailableError('auth_gate')`) belongs to a second session read taken only while `isAuthGateActive()` answers true, after the caller was resolved; that gate block sits behind REST's early `return undefined` for a caller with no `userId`, so when REST's first read fails the caller is anonymous and `enforceAuth` answers 401, never 503. The settings resolver has one read: its `getSession` closure feeds `resolveAuthzContext`, and `sessionUser` is captured off that same call. A read that fails resolves no caller, carries no posture, and meets the anonymous floor's 401, REST's answer in the same state. Storage's 503 arm exists because its reader was a new, separate read; nothing here is. The producer pin counts exactly one read per request. **Right.**

6. **Nothing admitted that was refused, nothing refused beyond the gate's definition.** The secure default resolver and any host resolver that sets no `authGate` meet an unchanged door; the un-held control pins 200 on every route with the service receiving that very context. A session user carries `authGate` only when plugin-auth's `computeAuthGate` returns a posture, which it does only while a gate feature is active, so the door's "refuse whenever the context carries `authGate`" is not wider in practice than REST's `isAuthGateActive()`-guarded re-read, the observation 6142166159 already recorded. An API-key caller never reaches the `getSession` closure in `resolveAuthzContext` (the key is admitted first; the session path runs only when no key resolved a user), so it carries no posture and is unchanged. **Right.**

7. **The pins measure the change.** A census read off the registration with a count equal to `SETTINGS_ROUTE_LEDGER`, each route named by the service member it calls on a served request; held under both postures, plus an async resolver and an allow-listed base, asserting status, `error.code`, the gate's message, no `data`, and a proxied service never reached; the un-held control; and the producer booted through `init`, `start` and `kernel:ready` with a counted session read and the context's `authGate` equal to `normalizeAuthGate(sessionUser)`. The two-leg ablation table is the dev's reading; the check-runs are the verdicts.

### ② Semver level

- **Level and carriers match what the diff publishes.** The diff both widens (one optional member on an exported interface) and narrows an accept set (a held session refused). `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is the grammar's spelling for exactly that case (`scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`: a diff that widens one surface and narrows another; `no (widening)` is the malformed one). `yes` requires at least `minor` on a package whose published source moved; the changeset grades `@objectstack/service-settings` `minor`, the only package touched, and carries the BREAKING banner and the `fix(service-settings)!:` summary, the launch-window carriers `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` names. No `major` (nothing removed, renamed or re-shaped), no `patch` admissible for a breaking narrowing, no second package. **Right**, and the same grading PR #23200 landed for the four siblings.
- **ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` fits.** The body's "What changes for you" paragraph is remediation advice for a held user and an opt-in note for a host authoring its own `contextFromRequest`; a resolver that never sets the field keeps every answer it had, so no consumer must rewrite anything to keep working. The other categories are closed on facts as the marker states. **Right.**
- **Gate verdicts off the head:** `Check Changeset` concludes `success` (the changeset-required, empty-frontmatter, no-major and ADR-0087 steps all run inside it); the dev's offline run of the two scripts against this PR body agrees.
- **PR form:** line 1 `Fixes #23178` is triage's direction (6142961139: the PR closes the card); `The card this PR closes must claim this branch`, `Part-of PR must not also close its card`, both single-writer guards and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` all conclude `success`.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every deviation and `out_of_scope_findings` entry of report 6147674138, plus what the inputs raised:

- **The field declared in `settings-service.types.ts`, not `settings-routes.ts` — answered.** The dispatch 6146033345 placed `SettingsContext` in the routes file; it is declared in the types file of the same package and imported from there by the routes file and the barrel. The change landed at the real declaration site, inside the claim's package and intent; the seat's ACCEPT 6147724004 records the same. No breach.
- **No label written — answered.** The package publishes and the PR carries a changeset, so `skip-changeset` would be false; the dispatch names no other label.
- **Attribution — answered.** All three commits end with the model-free pair (`Claude-Session:` plus `Co-authored-by: Claude`), which AGENTS.md prescribes and the pre-push hook enforces; the PR body carries the session-URL footer once. The repo rule outranks the harness reminder, as the dev read it.
- **Dist-reading gates first run on a partly built tree — answered.** The recorded exit codes are the re-runs on the built tree, and the verdicts of record are the head's check-runs (`Lint & Repo Gates` and `Build Core` conclude `success`), not the local run.
- **An API key beside a held session cookie — out of this card's scope; escalated as a cross-seam question, not blocking.** `resolveAuthzContext` admits the key first and takes the session path only when no key resolved a user, so this resolver, exactly like the datasource-admin and share-link resolvers PR #23200 landed (which review 6142166159 passed with "an API-key caller never reaches `getSession` so carries no posture"), carries no posture for that request. REST differs only because its gate re-read is cookie-driven and runs after key admission; REST admits the same held user's key alone. ADR-0069's text holds a session (a session for a user without two-factor is marked un-stepped-up), and a key is a different credential, so the family's answer is the gate as written. Whether a held cookie beside an admitted key should be refused at every seam is a parity question about `resolveAuthzContext` against REST, shared by all five raw-host families on `main` and pre-existing on four of them; it is the seat's to file as one cross-seam finding, if at all, with a ruling on session-versus-user. Not a property of this head.
- **`ExecutionContext.authGate.code` cast to `ErrorCode` — answered.** The same sink-side narrowing the four sibling doors carry, with the one producer writing only `PASSWORD_EXPIRED` and `MFA_REQUIRED`; an acceptance note is the right carrier, as 6142166159 already judged.
- **Docs drift (advisory run 6147651038) — residual for the seat, not blocking.** The runtime-services settings page names `SettingsContext` only in method signatures, so it is not falsified. The authentication page's "how enforcement works" paragraph still names the REST server and the runtime dispatcher as the seams that block a gated session; it predates PR #23200 and is now one landing further behind. A docs-only follow-up, outside this card's file surface.
- **Serial: #23174 shares `settings-routes.ts` — answered.** The dispatch and the ACCEPT both order it after this landing; nothing to do on this head.
